compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
All seven rows use the same fictional consultation, information, disclosure permissions, deadline, and decision authority.

Either reviewer can consider both columns. Each row identifies one preference difference or complementary tasks that both can do.

| Same consultation and decision authority | INTP: possible emphasis | ISFJ: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clarifying an unclear comment | Check what claim about the proposal the resident is making | Ask which concern the resident wants the organizers to address | Complementary clarification tasks either reviewer can do |
| Reading the same survey report | What patterns across the recorded observations might explain the result? | What locations and conditions were actually surveyed and recorded? | S/N: possible connections and documented details |
| Weighing the same objection | Would the same criteria support accepting this objection in comparable cases? | How would accepting or rejecting it affect the residents involved? | T/F: consistent criteria and consequences for people |
| Comparing the same cost-sharing proposals | Does each option apply its criteria consistently to comparable households? | How would the same options affect households with different needs or resources? | T/F: consistent treatment and effects on people. Either reviewer can consider both. |
| Planning outreach under the same requirements | Keep several feasible times open while confirming availability | Agree on a provisional schedule within the same limits | J/P: open options and provisional outward structure |
| Recording the same meeting | Record unresolved issues and what evidence is still needed | Record commitments, next steps, and who is accountable | Complementary tasks. Either reviewer can record both. |
| Reviewing the same verified outcomes later | How do the outcomes compare with the same evaluation criteria used at the start? | What do the verified outcomes mean for the people affected? | T/F: consistent criteria and consequences for people |

An experienced INTP may know what to ask residents, and an ISFJ may know which requirement to verify. Experience and assigned duty can explain those choices. The table cannot establish type or ability.
compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional residents’ meeting, two volunteers stay to stack chairs. Either may have participated actively or listened quietly. The circumstances and their responsibilities can explain those actions.

Shared Introversion concerns where attention and energy tend to go. It cannot determine how much someone speaks or what they think about a proposal.

Keep the three questions separate: what information carries weight (S/N), what criteria matter in a decision (T/F), and what arrangements should be settled or kept open (J/P). Any one proposal may involve all three questions.

### INTP and ISFJ: one sentence, this building cannot take a lift, and where each kind of ground comes from

In this fictional elevator consultation, both reviewers receive the same comment: “This won’t work in our building.” Both have the same consultation materials and authority.

One response asks what the available report confirms and what remains uncertain. Another asks whether the concern is about access, cost, or another effect on residents. Either reviewer can ask both questions before considering an arrangement.

A report cannot tell you which issue the resident meant. A resident’s concern cannot establish technical feasibility. The organizers can clarify the concern and refer technical questions to the qualified assessment team.

An ISFJ can question how the evidence was collected, and an INTP can raise an access concern. Either person can use both approaches. The timing of either question does not establish type.

Write down what was verified, what was inferred, and what would change the decision. This helps clarify which questions still need answers. It does not determine anyone’s type.

### INTP and ISFJ: same four names, two exchanges of seats

Both types are introverted, so their outward-facing process is auxiliary in type dynamics. INTP’s P points to extraverted Intuition (Ne), which supports dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). ISFJ’s J points to extraverted Feeling (Fe), which supports dominant introverted Sensing (Si).

In this notation, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The first and third positions trade places, as do the second and fourth. Reading INTP’s sequence backward gives Fe–Si–Ne–Ti, the corresponding notation for ESFJ.

The positions describe function roles in the model. They cannot tell you which contribution someone will make or when they will make it.

The Foundation lists tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si) and tertiary Thinking for ISFJ (Te or Ti). This page uses Si and Ti, so all four process names match in this convention. The alternatives leave the dominant and auxiliary processes unchanged. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and [ISFJ profile](/en/personality/isfj).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Both scenarios are fictional. They show how people can weigh information and options. Assign responsibilities according to relevant knowledge, access, and permission.

Both reviewers need to know what the proposal establishes and which concerns remain open. Use a shared summary, keeping personal information with the people authorized to handle it.

### INTP and ISFJ: reviewing a proposal to add an elevator

In this fictional six-story building, both reviewers have the same proposed cost-sharing options and the same anonymized feedback. One question is whether the options use a consistent rule. Another is how the options could affect residents with different needs.

A comparison of costs cannot show what residents think about the proposal. Resident feedback cannot settle whether the cost model was applied consistently. Both checks can help the organizers ask better questions.

Record verified information, unresolved questions, and who can follow up. Follow the building’s approved process for outreach and do not circulate residents’ personal details. This record shows project status, not personality.

### INTP and ISFJ: clearing the old family house, by usefulness or by who used it

In this fictional example, two relatives have the same list of items from a family home. One way to assess each item is to apply the same criteria for condition, likely use, and effort to move it. Another is to ask who values it and what family memories it carries.

Both relatives can consider the usefulness and history of each item. A shared list can show where they agree and where they need more information. Confirm who has the authority to decide before making commitments.

An INTP can ask relatives what matters to them, and an ISFJ can apply the same condition criteria across the list. Neither a sentimental moment nor a brisk decision can identify a type.

Who checks a report or responds to a concern first depends on responsibilities and available information. Either person may reverse the order on another project. It does not establish type.

comparison.summary:
INTP and ISFJ share Introversion (I). They differ on Sensing/Intuition, Thinking/Feeling, and Judging/Perceiving. These pairs concern information, decision criteria, and outward arrangements, respectively.

- **I (shared):** Introversion describes attention and energy directed more toward inner ideas and reflection. It does not tell you how much someone speaks or whether they have an opinion.
- **S/N:** ISFJ’s Sensing emphasizes observable details and relevant experience. INTP’s Intuition emphasizes connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **T/F:** INTP’s Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. ISFJ’s Feeling emphasizes values and the effects of a decision on people. Either type can consider both.
- **J/P:** ISFJ’s Judging favors outward structure and closure. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The processes in positions one and three switch, as do those in positions two and four. The full overlap depends on the notation for the tertiary attitudes.

Either type can check conditions, ask how people would be affected, or suggest a plan. The model cannot establish who acts first or how two people will work together.

- **I (shared):** Introversion describes attention and energy directed more toward inner ideas and reflection. It does not tell you how much someone speaks or whether they have an opinion.
- **S/N:** ISFJ’s Sensing emphasizes observable details and relevant experience. INTP’s Intuition emphasizes connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **T/F:** INTP’s Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. ISFJ’s Feeling emphasizes values and the effects of a decision on people. Either type can consider both.
- **J/P:** ISFJ’s Judging favors outward structure and closure. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The processes in positions one and three switch, as do those in positions two and four. The full overlap depends on the notation for the tertiary attitudes.

compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
All seven rows use the same fictional consultation, information, disclosure permissions, deadline, and decision authority.

Either reviewer can consider both columns. Each row identifies one preference difference or complementary tasks that both can do.

| Same consultation and decision authority | INTP: possible emphasis | ISFJ: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clarifying an unclear comment | Check what claim about the proposal the resident is making | Ask which concern the resident wants the organizers to address | Complementary clarification tasks either reviewer can do |
| Reading the same survey report | What patterns across the recorded observations might explain the result? | What locations and conditions were actually surveyed and recorded? | S/N: possible connections and documented details |
| Weighing the same objection | Would the same criteria support accepting this objection in comparable cases? | How would accepting or rejecting it affect the residents involved? | T/F: consistent criteria and consequences for people |
| Comparing the same cost-sharing proposals | Does each option apply its criteria consistently to comparable households? | How would the same options affect households with different needs or resources? | T/F: consistent treatment and effects on people. Either reviewer can consider both. |
| Planning outreach under the same requirements | Keep several feasible times open while confirming availability | Agree on a provisional schedule within the same limits | J/P: open options and provisional outward structure |
| Recording the same meeting | Record unresolved issues and what evidence is still needed | Record commitments, next steps, and who is accountable | Complementary tasks. Either reviewer can record both. |
| Reviewing the same verified outcomes later | How do the outcomes compare with the same evaluation criteria used at the start? | What do the verified outcomes mean for the people affected? | T/F: consistent criteria and consequences for people |

An experienced INTP may know what to ask residents, and an ISFJ may know which requirement to verify. Experience and assigned duty can explain those choices. The table cannot establish type or ability.
compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional residents’ meeting, two volunteers stay to stack chairs. Either may have participated actively or listened quietly. The circumstances and their responsibilities can explain those actions.

Shared Introversion concerns where attention and energy tend to go. It cannot determine how much someone speaks or what they think about a proposal.

Keep the three questions separate: what information carries weight (S/N), what criteria matter in a decision (T/F), and what arrangements should be settled or kept open (J/P). Any one proposal may involve all three questions.

### INTP and ISFJ: one sentence, this building cannot take a lift, and where each kind of ground comes from

In this fictional elevator consultation, both reviewers receive the same comment: “This won’t work in our building.” Both have the same consultation materials and authority.

One response asks what the available report confirms and what remains uncertain. Another asks whether the concern is about access, cost, or another effect on residents. Either reviewer can ask both questions before considering an arrangement.

A report cannot tell you which issue the resident meant. A resident’s concern cannot establish technical feasibility. The organizers can clarify the concern and refer technical questions to the qualified assessment team.

An ISFJ can question how the evidence was collected, and an INTP can raise an access concern. Either person can use both approaches. The timing of either question does not establish type.

Write down what was verified, what was inferred, and what would change the decision. This helps clarify which questions still need answers. It does not determine anyone’s type.

### INTP and ISFJ: same four names, two exchanges of seats

Both types are introverted, so their outward-facing process is auxiliary in type dynamics. INTP’s P points to extraverted Intuition (Ne), which supports dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). ISFJ’s J points to extraverted Feeling (Fe), which supports dominant introverted Sensing (Si).

In this notation, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The first and third positions trade places, as do the second and fourth. Reading INTP’s sequence backward gives Fe–Si–Ne–Ti, the corresponding notation for ESFJ.

The positions describe function roles in the model. They cannot tell you which contribution someone will make or when they will make it.

The Foundation lists tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si) and tertiary Thinking for ISFJ (Te or Ti). This page uses Si and Ti, so all four process names match in this convention. The alternatives leave the dominant and auxiliary processes unchanged. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and [ISFJ profile](/en/personality/isfj).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Both scenarios are fictional. They show how people can weigh information and options. Assign responsibilities according to relevant knowledge, access, and permission.

Both reviewers need to know what the proposal establishes and which concerns remain open. Use a shared summary, keeping personal information with the people authorized to handle it.

### INTP and ISFJ: reviewing a proposal to add an elevator

In this fictional six-story building, both reviewers have the same proposed cost-sharing options and the same anonymized feedback. One question is whether the options use a consistent rule. Another is how the options could affect residents with different needs.

A comparison of costs cannot show what residents think about the proposal. Resident feedback cannot settle whether the cost model was applied consistently. Both checks can help the organizers ask better questions.

Record verified information, unresolved questions, and who can follow up. Follow the building’s approved process for outreach and do not circulate residents’ personal details. This record shows project status, not personality.

### INTP and ISFJ: clearing the old family house, by usefulness or by who used it

In this fictional example, two relatives have the same list of items from a family home. One way to assess each item is to apply the same criteria for condition, likely use, and effort to move it. Another is to ask who values it and what family memories it carries.

Both relatives can consider the usefulness and history of each item. A shared list can show where they agree and where they need more information. Confirm who has the authority to decide before making commitments.

An INTP can ask relatives what matters to them, and an ISFJ can apply the same condition criteria across the list. Neither a sentimental moment nor a brisk decision can identify a type.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Introversion concerns where attention and energy tend to go. Being quiet in a meeting does not mean a person has no opinion.

Thinking and Feeling concern criteria in a decision. They cannot tell you whether someone cares about others or how they handle pressure.

Who checks a report or responds to a concern first depends on responsibilities and available information. Either person may reverse the order on another project. It does not establish type.

faq_blocks.answer:
They share I and differ on S/N, T/F, and J/P.

S/N concerns observable details and experience or patterns and possibilities. T/F concerns consistent criteria or values and effects on people. J/P concerns outward structure or keeping options open. One decision can involve all three without revealing someone’s type.
faq_blocks.question: Which letters differ between INTP and ISFJ?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. In the notation used here, both stacks contain the same four processes, but those processes have different roles.

INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne in this convention. The first and third positions switch, as do the second and fourth. The Foundation’s tertiary alternatives can change which processes overlap. No position establishes action order or ability.
faq_blocks.question: Same four function names — can they still be two types?

faq_blocks.answer:
Either type can question data and consider how a proposal affects people.

Training and responsibilities can explain who checks the evidence. Access and the needs of others can explain who follows up. What someone does in one meeting does not establish a preference.
faq_blocks.question: ISFJ also presses on data, INTP also looks after people — how should such counterexamples be handled?

faq_blocks.answer:
Both checking the proposal and contacting residents may be needed. Assign those tasks to people with the relevant information, authority, and time.

Record which questions need answers and who is responsible for the next update. Keep private contact information in the authorized process. Either person can handle either role.
faq_blocks.question: In something like a residents' meeting, which stretch does each hold?

faq_blocks.answer:
One possible problem is mismatched expectations about when a reply is due.

Agree when to acknowledge a request, when to provide an answer, and who should follow up. If replies keep slipping, check whether responsibilities or information are unclear.
faq_blocks.question: Working with either of them long term, where does it most often jam?

faq_blocks.answer:
First check whether the instrument, version, language, and scoring guidance match.

If the same instrument gives interpretable scores, use its guidance for S/N, T/F, and J/P separately. Different labels alone cannot show whether the scores were near a cutoff or why they changed.

- **T/F:** INTP’s Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. ISFJ’s Feeling emphasizes values and the effects of a decision on people. Either type can consider both.
- **J/P:** ISFJ’s Judging favors outward structure and closure. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The processes in positions one and three switch, as do those in positions two and four. The full overlap depends on the notation for the tertiary attitudes.

Either type can check conditions, ask how people would be affected, or suggest a plan. The model cannot establish who acts first or how two people will work together.

sections.body_md:
INTP and ISFJ share Introversion (I). They differ on Sensing/Intuition, Thinking/Feeling, and Judging/Perceiving. These pairs concern information, decision criteria, and outward arrangements, respectively.

- **I (shared):** Introversion describes attention and energy directed more toward inner ideas and reflection. It does not tell you how much someone speaks or whether they have an opinion.
- **S/N:** ISFJ’s Sensing emphasizes observable details and relevant experience. INTP’s Intuition emphasizes connections, patterns, and possibilities.
- **T/F:** INTP’s Thinking emphasizes principles and consistently applied criteria. ISFJ’s Feeling emphasizes values and the effects of a decision on people. Either type can consider both.
- **J/P:** ISFJ’s Judging favors outward structure and closure. INTP’s Perceiving favors keeping options open to new information. Either person can make or revise a plan.

In the notation used here, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The processes in positions one and three switch, as do those in positions two and four. The full overlap depends on the notation for the tertiary attitudes.

Either type can check conditions, ask how people would be affected, or suggest a plan. The model cannot establish who acts first or how two people will work together.
sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
In a fictional residents’ meeting, two volunteers stay to stack chairs. Either may have participated actively or listened quietly. The circumstances and their responsibilities can explain those actions.

Shared Introversion concerns where attention and energy tend to go. It cannot determine how much someone speaks or what they think about a proposal.

Keep the three questions separate: what information carries weight (S/N), what criteria matter in a decision (T/F), and what arrangements should be settled or kept open (J/P). Any one proposal may involve all three questions.

### INTP and ISFJ: one sentence, this building cannot take a lift, and where each kind of ground comes from

In this fictional elevator consultation, both reviewers receive the same comment: “This won’t work in our building.” Both have the same consultation materials and authority.

One response asks what the available report confirms and what remains uncertain. Another asks whether the concern is about access, cost, or another effect on residents. Either reviewer can ask both questions before considering an arrangement.

A report cannot tell you which issue the resident meant. A resident’s concern cannot establish technical feasibility. The organizers can clarify the concern and refer technical questions to the qualified assessment team.

An ISFJ can question how the evidence was collected, and an INTP can raise an access concern. Either person can use both approaches. The timing of either question does not establish type.

Write down what was verified, what was inferred, and what would change the decision. This helps clarify which questions still need answers. It does not determine anyone’s type.

### INTP and ISFJ: same four names, two exchanges of seats

Both types are introverted, so their outward-facing process is auxiliary in type dynamics. INTP’s P points to extraverted Intuition (Ne), which supports dominant introverted Thinking (Ti). ISFJ’s J points to extraverted Feeling (Fe), which supports dominant introverted Sensing (Si).

In this notation, INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The first and third positions trade places, as do the second and fourth. Reading INTP’s sequence backward gives Fe–Si–Ne–Ti, the corresponding notation for ESFJ.

The positions describe function roles in the model. They cannot tell you which contribution someone will make or when they will make it.

The Foundation lists tertiary Sensing for INTP (Se or Si) and tertiary Thinking for ISFJ (Te or Ti). This page uses Si and Ti, so all four process names match in this convention. The alternatives leave the dominant and auxiliary processes unchanged. See the [INTP profile](/en/personality/intp) and [ISFJ profile](/en/personality/isfj).
sections.title: INTP and ISFJ: what they share, and where the three axes differ

sections.body_md:
All seven rows use the same fictional consultation, information, disclosure permissions, deadline, and decision authority.

Either reviewer can consider both columns. Each row identifies one preference difference or complementary tasks that both can do.

| Same consultation and decision authority | INTP: possible emphasis | ISFJ: possible emphasis | What the row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clarifying an unclear comment | Check what claim about the proposal the resident is making | Ask which concern the resident wants the organizers to address | Complementary clarification tasks either reviewer can do |
| Reading the same survey report | What patterns across the recorded observations might explain the result? | What locations and conditions were actually surveyed and recorded? | S/N: possible connections and documented details |
| Weighing the same objection | Would the same criteria support accepting this objection in comparable cases? | How would accepting or rejecting it affect the residents involved? | T/F: consistent criteria and consequences for people |
| Comparing the same cost-sharing proposals | Does each option apply its criteria consistently to comparable households? | How would the same options affect households with different needs or resources? | T/F: consistent treatment and effects on people. Either reviewer can consider both. |
| Planning outreach under the same requirements | Keep several feasible times open while confirming availability | Agree on a provisional schedule within the same limits | J/P: open options and provisional outward structure |
| Recording the same meeting | Record unresolved issues and what evidence is still needed | Record commitments, next steps, and who is accountable | Complementary tasks. Either reviewer can record both. |
| Reviewing the same verified outcomes later | How do the outcomes compare with the same evaluation criteria used at the start? | What do the verified outcomes mean for the people affected? | T/F: consistent criteria and consequences for people |

An experienced INTP may know what to ask residents, and an ISFJ may know which requirement to verify. Experience and assigned duty can explain those choices. The table cannot establish type or ability.
sections.title: INTP and ISFJ in one minute

sections.body_md:
Both scenarios are fictional. They show how people can weigh information and options. Assign responsibilities according to relevant knowledge, access, and permission.

Both reviewers need to know what the proposal establishes and which concerns remain open. Use a shared summary, keeping personal information with the people authorized to handle it.

### INTP and ISFJ: reviewing a proposal to add an elevator

In this fictional six-story building, both reviewers have the same proposed cost-sharing options and the same anonymized feedback. One question is whether the options use a consistent rule. Another is how the options could affect residents with different needs.

A comparison of costs cannot show what residents think about the proposal. Resident feedback cannot settle whether the cost model was applied consistently. Both checks can help the organizers ask better questions.

Record verified information, unresolved questions, and who can follow up. Follow the building’s approved process for outreach and do not circulate residents’ personal details. This record shows project status, not personality.

### INTP and ISFJ: clearing the old family house, by usefulness or by who used it

In this fictional example, two relatives have the same list of items from a family home. One way to assess each item is to apply the same criteria for condition, likely use, and effort to move it. Another is to ask who values it and what family memories it carries.

Both relatives can consider the usefulness and history of each item. A shared list can show where they agree and where they need more information. Confirm who has the authority to decide before making commitments.

An INTP can ask relatives what matters to them, and an ISFJ can apply the same condition criteria across the list. Neither a sentimental moment nor a brisk decision can identify a type.

sections.body_md:
Introversion concerns where attention and energy tend to go. Being quiet in a meeting does not mean a person has no opinion.

Thinking and Feeling concern criteria in a decision. They cannot tell you whether someone cares about others or how they handle pressure.

Who checks a report or responds to a concern first depends on responsibilities and available information. Either person may reverse the order on another project. It does not establish type.
sections.title: INTP and ISFJ: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
Compare the instrument, version, language, and scoring guidance. Consider which situations you had in mind. Different roles can affect which examples you recall without establishing that a preference changed.

If comparable reports give interpretable scores, review S/N, T/F, and J/P one at a time using the instrument’s guidance. The labels alone cannot show whether a score was near a cutoff or why it changed.

Recall several comparable decisions where you had some choice. Note the information you used, the criteria that mattered, and whether you agreed on a provisional arrangement or kept options open. The notes support reflection and cannot determine a type.
sections.title: INTP and ISFJ: how to keep observing

items.answer:
They share I and differ on S/N, T/F, and J/P.

S/N concerns observable details and experience or patterns and possibilities. T/F concerns consistent criteria or values and effects on people. J/P concerns outward structure or keeping options open. One decision can involve all three without revealing someone’s type.
items.question: Which letters differ between INTP and ISFJ?

items.answer:
Yes. In the notation used here, both stacks contain the same four processes, but those processes have different roles.

INTP is Ti–Ne–Si–Fe and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne in this convention. The first and third positions switch, as do the second and fourth. The Foundation’s tertiary alternatives can change which processes overlap. No position establishes action order or ability.
items.question: Same four function names — can they still be two types?

items.answer:
Either type can question data and consider how a proposal affects people.

Training and responsibilities can explain who checks the evidence. Access and the needs of others can explain who follows up. What someone does in one meeting does not establish a preference.
items.question: ISFJ also presses on data, INTP also looks after people — how should such counterexamples be handled?

items.answer:
Both checking the proposal and contacting residents may be needed. Assign those tasks to people with the relevant information, authority, and time.

Record which questions need answers and who is responsible for the next update. Keep private contact information in the authorized process. Either person can handle either role.
items.question: In something like a residents' meeting, which stretch does each hold?

items.answer:
One possible problem is mismatched expectations about when a reply is due.

Agree when to acknowledge a request, when to provide an answer, and who should follow up. If replies keep slipping, check whether responsibilities or information are unclear.
items.question: Working with either of them long term, where does it most often jam?

items.answer:
First check whether the instrument, version, language, and scoring guidance match.

If the same instrument gives interpretable scores, use its guidance for S/N, T/F, and J/P separately. Different labels alone cannot show whether the scores were near a cutoff or why they changed.

**Framework sources**: the definitions of the preferences follow the [Myers-Briggs official facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); the type-dynamics framework follows the [Foundation's note on type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

**Function notation:** This page uses Ti–Ne–Si–Fe for INTP and Si–Fe–Ti–Ne for ISFJ. The Foundation gives alternatives for both tertiary attitudes. The first two positions in each stack are unchanged.

**Fictional examples:** The elevator consultation and family-home case illustrate how people can use the same information and weigh different concerns. They describe no real event and do not establish anyone’s type.

**Scope limits**: this page cites no statistical data and offers no behavioural prediction for any type. Results are not for ranking ability, hiring screens or predicting relationships; medical, emergency, legal and financial judgements belong with the relevant professionals. The FermatMind assessment uses a separate item bank and scoring; its scope is set out in the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
